fig:correction-cokernel-example.title: A specified correction range in $\mathbb R^2$. For $L(a,b)=(a,0)$, the image is the horizontal axis. The defect $(2,3)$ splits into $(2,0)$ in that image and the remaining representative $(0,3)$. Subtracting the image component leaves the same cokernel class. The functional $(x,y)\mapsto y$ vanishes on the correction range and detects the value three. The correction equation $Lu=-(2,3)$ therefore has no solution

fig:rotating-projector-example.title: A rotating rank one packet and its orthogonal complement. With $u(\theta )=(\cos \theta ,\sin \theta )$ and $P(\theta )=u(\theta )u(\theta )^{\mathsf T}$, the canonical generator is $[P',P]=\bigl (\begin {smallmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end {smallmatrix}\bigr )$. For a positive step $\delta <\pi /2$, the polar unitary is the usual rotation $R(\delta )$. On each displayed mesh, the direct rotation product equals $R(\pi /3)$ exactly. This special planar example illustrates the construction. The general theorem supplies convergence for families whose step products need not already equal the continuous transport
